applicability.reason: Held, with the blocker RE-MEASURED and narrowed AGAIN. Three of the four pieces now exist and are tested at the Rust level. (1) The heap stores objects in relocatable slots and `compact` really moves them. (2) `reachable_from` traces the WHOLE object graph, crossing between the heap and the Arc-backed Array and Hash bodies, terminating on cycles, and following raw ivars - which live in a runtime side table rather than the heap payload, and whose omission was caught by a test asserting a REACHABLE cycle survives. (3) `Runtime::collect_garbage` sweeps `owned - reachable` and then compacts; a unit test observes exactly what this row claims - a surviving object keeps its identity hash across a collection that frees a neighbour and MOVES the survivor into the freed slot (freed 1, moved 1). What is still missing is the ROOT SET at source level. Local bindings are a `&HashMap<String, Value>` parameter threaded through evaluation (14 signatures), not evaluator-owned state, so a `compact_gc()` called inside a method body cannot enumerate the locals of its enclosing frames - they are on the Rust stack. Exposing a FREEING collector to Iris source would therefore free live objects. `NativeFixture.compact_gc` stays relocation-only and answers 0, so wiring this row on it would still make its central claim vacuous. Closing it needs the evaluator to own an explicit frame stack; that is a refactor of the evaluator's calling convention, and the VM will redefine frame representation anyway.
